units.summary: The meeting notes record an estimate of about 1,200 freight documents per day across all sites, to be checked against volume data because the TMS log may differ.
units.quote: Mikko estimated about 1,200 documents per day across all sites. (To be checked against the volume data Jari will send - the TMS log may give a different number.)

units.summary: A meeting participant estimated that the TMS document log showed around 1,000 documents on a normal working day, noting that the log counts paper documents when scanned.
units.quote: I would say it's a bit less, maybe around 1,000 on a normal working day according to the TMS document log. But the log only counts paper documents when they are scanned, so it depends on how you count.

units.summary: Freight document processing is the company's highest-priority AI use case. Manual entry errors cause invoice corrections and disputes, while missed handwritten damage remarks can delay claims against hauliers.
units.quote: Mikko's estimate of the error rate in manual entry: around 4 %. Errors lead to wrong invoices, credit notes, and disputes; the finance team spends "a day a week" on corrections.

units.summary: The desired process is to extract document fields into the TMS and have a person check only low-confidence documents, with handwritten remarks flagged.
units.quote: Desired outcome: automatic extraction of the fields into the TMS with a human check only for low-confidence documents; flagging of handwritten remarks.

units.summary: The advisors said vision language models could handle mixed-quality photos and multilingual documents, but identified handwriting as the main risk to test on real samples.
units.quote: modern vision language models handle mixed-quality photos and multilingual documents reasonably well. Handwriting is the main risk; must be tested on real samples.

units.summary: The advisors proposed starting the document-processing pilot with PODs at the Vantaa site before scaling.
units.quote: Start with one document type (POD) and one site (Vantaa) before scaling.

units.summary: The TMS has an API for individual records, and bulk export is a paid service.
units.quote: REST API, single records; bulk export as paid service

units.summary: Document clerks enter freight-document information in the TMS and enter invoicing-relevant data again in Business Central.
units.quote: Invoicing-relevant data is also entered in Business Central.

units.summary: The current workflow includes manual data entry of packages, weight, pallets, date, signature and remarks, with an estimated 3–4 minutes per document and about 4% errors.
units.quote:
Packages, weight, pallets, date, signature, remarks  
3–4 min / doc ~4 % errors

units.summary: The proposed forecasting use case is to predict daily inbound pallets and outbound order lines per warehouse one to three weeks ahead, using WMS history and customer forecasts, with calendar effects and possibly weather as inputs.
units.quote: Idea: forecast daily inbound pallets and outbound order lines per warehouse 1-3 weeks ahead, using history from the WMS plus customer forecasts, calendar effects (holidays, campaigns), and maybe weather for the chilled food customers.

units.summary: The WMS has six years of history, but comparability of pre-2020 data is uncertain; Oulu data starts in 2023.
units.quote: Six years of history exist in the WMS, but the system was replaced/upgraded in 2020 and Jari is not sure whether pre-2020 data is comparable. Oulu has only data since 2023.

units.summary: Staffing is planned weekly using supervisors' experience and customer forecasts, and overtime costs were about EUR 410,000 in 2025; Tampere was identified as the worst-affected site due to irregular customer volumes.
units.quote: Overtime and last-minute agency staff are costly. Mikko: overtime costs were about EUR 410,000 in 2025, with the Tampere site the worst because of one large spare-parts customer with very irregular volumes.

units.summary: The proposed customer-service use case is to classify incoming emails, route them, retrieve shipment status from the TMS, and draft replies for an agent to approve.
units.quote: Idea: automatically classify incoming emails, route them, look up shipment status from the TMS and draft a reply for the agent to approve.

units.summary: The company was not seeking fully automatic replies at this stage; an agent would approve every answer, at least initially.
units.quote: But not fully automatic replies. The agent should approve every answer, at least in the beginning.

units.summary: Customer service uses a shared Outlook mailbox and has no ticketing system.
units.quote: Customer service: shared Outlook mailbox, no ticketing system.

units.summary: Customer-service emails contain consumer personal data, and GDPR and AI Act transparency questions were raised about access and data processing.
units.quote: Emails contain personal data (names, phone numbers, home delivery addresses of consumers for e-commerce customers). GDPR and AI Act transparency questions came up - who can see what, where the data is processed.

units.summary: The advisors considered email triage relatively easy technically but more compliance-intensive, and suggested it as a second step after an AI policy is in place.
units.quote: Email triage is relatively easy technically but has the most compliance work; good second step once an AI policy exists.

units.summary: The TMS has a route-planning module used for Vantaa-area distribution, but planners often override it because it does not account for customers' unloading times.
units.quote: The TMS has a built-in route planning module. Planners use it for Vantaa-area distribution but override it often because "it does not know the customers' unloading times".

units.summary: Route optimisation using actual unloading times was mentioned as another idea, and the TMS vendor might provide an update in 2027.
units.quote: Route optimisation using real unloading times (TMS vendor may provide an update in 2027).

units.summary: Predictive maintenance for trucks and forklifts was mentioned as an idea; telematics data exists, but the fleet manager was not present.
units.quote: Predictive maintenance for trucks and forklifts (telematics data exists, but the fleet manager was not present).

units.summary: Automatic customs declarations were mentioned as an idea, but Kaisa considered them too risky for now.
units.quote: Automatic generation of customs declarations - Kaisa sees this as too risky for now.

units.summary: The company has no machine-learning models in production and has no data warehouse; reporting uses Excel exports and a few Power BI reports maintained by Jari.
units.quote: No machine learning models in production. No data warehouse; reporting is done in Excel exports and a few Power BI reports that Jari maintains.

conflicts.description: The meeting notes give an estimate of about 1,200 documents per day across all sites. The recording gives an estimate of around 1,000 on a normal working day based on the TMS log, with a caveat that paper documents are counted when scanned. The sources provide no hierarchy that resolves the differing estimates.
